newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bearish mood persists in Nigerian stocks trade.
newsitem.headline: Bearish mood persists in Nigerian stocks trade.

text.p: Nigeria's stock trade ended down again on Thursday on persistent bearish mood, dealers said.
The all-share index fell to 8350.91 from 8374.66 on Wednesday.
Dealers said investors were still dumping shares on fears they would slide further.
"There is no money in the country now. That is why many people are selling," said one dealer.
The trend has persisted longer than expected because of poor financial results the companies were returning, according to analysts.
Shares of blue chip companies, whose prices have soared tremendously in recent months, are crumbling as most investors rush to cut their losses.
Among losers on Thursday was conglomerate UAC, which reported lower first quarter profit to end-March 1997.
UAC posted 95 million naira against 117 million naira in the corresponding 1996 period. It closed 15 naira, down 10 kobo.
Flour Mills was steady on Thursday at 16 after its full year result calmed market fears on its performance in the year ended December 31, 1996.
Profit after taxation fell to 412.4 million naira from 471.1 million naira in the preceding year.
But Lever Brothers dropped to 26 naira after shedding 30 kobo. Nigerian Bottling Co fell 15 kobo to 51.50 naira and Nigerian Breweries finished 10 down at 17.70 naira.

Other big losers were PZ Industries, which closed six kobo lower at 25.94 naira and First Bank at 12.80 naira, down 10 kobo. Oil marketers continued their slide as investors were disinterested in buying the large quantities flooding the market.
African Petroleum and Unipetrol were each down 50 kobo at 53 naira and 65.50 naira, respectively.
Gains were led by Guinness, which also posted steady first quarter profit to end-March 1997.
The brewing stock closed at 8.15 naira, up 10 kobo.
NCR was up 15 kobo at 12.85 naira and Neimeth Pharmaceuticals, up 10 kobo at 7.90 naira on its recent good half-year result.
Paint company IPWA came back from loss on Thursday and dealers rewarded it with a three kobo rise to 1.73 naira.
